messages.author: aa1c1fa1a43b4d47
messages.subject: Generalized logistic model problem in Rstan
parts:
I'm fitting a 4 parameter logistic-type model described in http://bioinformatics.oxfordjournals.org/content/27/5/707.full (using their 5 parameter model but without the "E" parameter). Command-line compilation on 64-bit linux works great and usually converges to reasonable values. Rstan compiles it just fine but fails to run the model unless I init with values close to the end values:

Error : Error in function stan::prob::lognormal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Location parameter is -nan:0, but must be finite!
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

The model is below:
data {
 int<lower=0> N;
 real y[N];
 real<upper=0> logDose[N];
}
parameters {
 real A;
 real<upper=A> B;
 real<upper=0> C;
 real D;
 real<lower=0> s;
}
model {
 A ~ normal(0,100);
 B ~ normal(0,100);
 C ~ normal(0,100);
 D ~ normal(0,100);
 s ~ lognormal(0,1);
 for ( i in 1:N ) {
   real f;
   f <- B + (A-B)/(1+pow(logDose[i]/C,D));
   y[i] ~ lognormal( log(f), s );
 }
}

I know that in my data, logDose is always negative & B is pinned to be no greater than A, so f (and log f) should always be positive.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Generalized logistic model problem in Rstan
parts:
I'm glad to hear at least one version works :-)

They should behave identically if you're using the
1.3 versions of each with the same compilers. Are
you running 64-bit R on Linux, too?

If you're using a later version of either, they won't
necessarily be in synch again until the 2.0 release (which
should be soon). We've been making numerical stability
improvements in things like the distributions (can't recall
if we hit log normal or one of its components or not).

As something to do later, you could speed the main loop up
in the model considerably by vectorizing the call
and only computing (A - B) once.

{
real AminusB;
vector[N] log_f;
AminusB <- A - B;
for (n in 1:N)
log_f[n] <- log(B + AminusB / (1 + pow(logDose[i]/C, D)));
y ~ lognormal(log_f, s);
}


In Stan, calls to probability functions are expensive,
whereas assignments, allocations and loops are cheap.

- Bob

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Generalized logistic model problem in Rstan
parts:
Hi!

Shouldn't the expression

for (n in 1:N)
log_f[n] <- log(B + AminusB / (1 + pow(logDose[i]/C, D)));
be changed to
for (n in 1:N)

log_f[n] <- log(B + AminusB / (1 + pow(logDose[i] * Cinv, D)));

??? I mean dividing by a quantity which is sampled is always a bad thing to do for the sampler due to possible division by 0. I know that C is bounded to be below 0, but this doesn't exclude values very close to -0…

I am asking because I got used to coding with inverses, but sometimes I would prefer to avoid doing this. So I am wondering what your experience is with this kind of problem. Another approach I would probably use is to code it in log-space as
for (n in 1:N)

log_f[n] <- log(B + AminusB / (1 + pow(logDose[i] * exp(-CLog), D)));

… and of course not restrict Clog in its support. So what is best numerically wise?

Best,
Sebastian
